final_answer:
PRIVILEGED WORK PRODUCT - MEMORANDUM: Pinnacle MSJ (Greenfield v. Pinnacle, 5:23-cv-412-MTT, M.D. Ga.) - Prioritized Weaknesses

BOTTOM LINE
Denial should be achievable. Tier 1 flaws are dispositive: (1) the brief misquotes LSA ss. 7.1, 7.3 and 11.7, dropping the carve-outs and conditions that defeat its cap, waiver and force majeure arguments; (2) Pinnacle's own witness and SUMF concede facts creating genuine disputes on force majeure, gross negligence and mitigation; (3) the expert evidence is inconsistent and Ellington is unqualified on salvage. Realistic risk is limited to partial damages rulings (Section 11). Deadline: response due 21 days after service (L.R. 7.2, verified); service July 15, 2024, so Aug. 5, 2024 unless extended - confirm.

TIER 1 - DISPOSITIVE

1. Force majeure (s. 11.7)
- Actual s. 11.7 requires notice within 72 hours, written notice of the event, affected obligations and resumption steps, and updates. The brief's block quote omits all of it. Holt: no notice of the June, August or January failures; never thought about s. 11.7 (Holt 29-30, 41, 85). Santos 33-38: Greenfield learned nothing until Feb. 6, 2023. Defense is Pinnacle's burden; condition unmet.
- SUMF 13 adds "to the extent... impracticable" language not in the LSA; SUMF cites nonexistent "s. 12.1" and wrong sections (fees are s. 5.1, exclusivity s. 3.2).
- Not an act of God: June-August 2022 ran 2-4 degrees F above the 30-year average (SUMF 17; Venkatesh 5.3), not "record-breaking." Georgia defines act of God as an irresistible physical cause (O.C.G.A. s. 1-3-3(1); confirm text). No utility failure: SUMF 22; Holt 103.
- Cause was mechanical and budgetary: Holt 101 (refrigerant leaks, compressor, old unit); Aug. 9, 2022 email (Ex. 14): "We really need to replace the whole unit"; Okafor: "Get another patch. Replacement not in the budget until Q1 2023." Holt raised it four or five times (43). Budget choices are within Pinnacle's control.
- Ignored duties: s. 4.3 (backup climate control; 24-hour written notice of HVAC failure), s. 10.2(c) warranty, Ex. B para. 5. Only fans, no dehumidifiers, during 14- and 13-day outages and after Jan. 18, 2023 (Holt 29-30, 83; Venkatesh 3.7). The brief omits the Jan. 18 failure; Unit 3 was dead 2.5-3 weeks (Holt 83).
- "Commercially reasonable efforts" is a fact question; Okafor Decl. 5 (replacement lead time) ignores the budget refusal.

2. Liability cap (s. 7.1)
- Actual s. 7.1: the GREATER of 12 months' fees or $2,000,000, and it "shall not apply to claims arising from Pinnacle's gross negligence or willful misconduct." The brief's quoted text is not in the LSA. Cap is at least $2,000,000, not $1,860,000.
- s. 7.2 also exempts s. 9.1 indemnity (breach of ss. 4.1-4.6; contamination of Inventory; fees), gross negligence/willful misconduct, and claims Pinnacle must insure under Art. 6 (full-replacement property cover, s. 6.1(b)). Seek policies. Risk: Pinnacle may call s. 9.1 third-party-only; s. 9.1(b) and the fee language support first-party reach.
- Gross negligence (O.C.G.A. s. 51-1-4: absence of slight diligence) is a jury question: Okafor refused replacement despite written warning about $4.7M of inventory, ordered reports withheld, no dehumidification. Georgia authority lets gross negligence/willful misconduct defeat limitation clauses (secondary sources; verify controlling cases). Okafor Decl. 11's denial is a conclusion.
- Math conflicts: brief uses Feb. 2022-Jan. 2023; SUMF 14 uses July 2022-June 2023, ending after the claim and including withheld months (SUMF 15: $310,000 unpaid Jan.-Feb. 2023), so fees actually "paid" were about $1.55M; Ellington 28 calls $1.86M the total over "the term." "Claim first arose" may mean June 2022. s. 5.4 adjustments ignored. Brief cites SUMF 5 for "represented by counsel"; SUMF 5 says nothing of the kind.

3. Consequential-damages waiver (s. 7.3)
- Actual s. 7.3: "This waiver shall not apply to claims arising from a party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of Section 4.2." Brief and SUMF 12 quote different, longer language not in the LSA. Humidity of 72-85% versus the 60% limit is admitted (SUMF 36), so the $890,000 and $1,150,000 are outside the waiver.
- Expedited costs are also mitigation expenses (s. 7.4; O.C.G.A. s. 13-6-5); Pinnacle cannot fault non-mitigation and call mitigation costs consequential. O.C.G.A. s. 11-2-715 (sales) is inapposite to a warehousing-services contract (UCC Art. 7, s. 11-7-204; confirm). Ellington disclaims legal characterization (Dep. 46).
- Lost-profit "certainty" argument cites Ellington Decl. 10-12, which concern overhead; his lost-profit discussion is paras. 23-24.

4. Mitigation (s. 7.4; O.C.G.A. s. 13-6-5)
- s. 4.5 is a right, not a duty; ss. 4.2 and 4.5 call reporting "affirmative" and independent of inspection; s. 7.4 requires only commercially reasonable steps and no duty "to discover a breach that the other Party has concealed or failed to disclose." The brief never cites s. 7.4.
- Concealment: Holt: Okafor said in early Nov. 2022 "Hold off on the reports... No point in raising alarms," repeated in Dec.; data were "bad," upper 60s-70s (Holt 65-68, 99). Okafor Decl. 7: calibration delay; no recollection. Direct conflict is for the jury (Anderson, 477 U.S. at 255). Holt never told Greenfield of the Oct. 3 78% reading (58).
- Santos emailed Holt in December and January and was told reports were "coming" (Santos 33-38, 55-57), contradicting the brief, SUMF 31 and Ellington Decl. 20. His visits were logistics visits (24-29). SUMF 30's "no 48-hour notice" is irrelevant.
- Mitigation is Pinnacle's burden and usually factual. Ellington's "2-2.5 months earlier / 600-800 panels" (Decl. 22) lacks growth data and assumes degradation began "mid-September," contradicting the June 14 failure (SUMF 18; Holt 28-29).

5. Comparative fault (O.C.G.A. s. 51-12-33)
- Tort concept; no authority applying it to Count I. For Count II apportionment is factual and rests on the same disputed inspection theory. S. Gen. Ins. Co. v. Holt, 262 Ga. 267 (1992), is an insurer failure-to-settle case (verified), not apportionment. Denton v. Eaton unverified. Sensor-cost assertion has no expert support. Hargrove transcript not in our file; pull 112-117.

6. Unbriefed counts; Rule 56 defects
- Counts II and III are never analyzed; movant must show absence of a genuine dispute (Celotex, 477 U.S. at 323); Rule 56(a) requires identifying the part sought, yet the brief seeks "summary judgment on the damages issue" vaguely.
- Liability is effectively conceded: failures (SUMF 18-21), humidity breach (SUMF 36), missing reports (SUMF 25). Counterclaim ($340,000, including $30,000 late fees exceeding s. 5.3's $1,500/month) is unbriefed; plead prior material breach/setoff.

TIER 2 - SUBSTANTIAL

7. Expert evidence (Ellington)
- Dep. 14, 78-85: no science, remediation, IICRC or CIH credentials; never reviewed ANSI/IICRC S520 or wood-panel studies; two trade journals; defers to Venkatesh, whose conclusion was no salvage. Move under Fed. R. Evid. 702 (amended Dec. 1, 2023; verify text).
- Venkatesh: hyphae in 34 of 36 tape-lifts and all 18 swabs, moisture 22-35%, warping/delamination, S520/EPA porous-material guidance (3.5, 4.2, 4.5, 5.5). "Undisputed expert evidence" is false.
- Inconsistencies (Decl. July 12, 2024 versus Dep. Apr. 18, 2024 versus brief): salvage 30-40% / 25-30% / 35-45%; incremental cost $1,680 / $1,780 / $1,750; Dep. $940,000-$1,175,000 does not match 25-30% of $4.7M ($1.175M-$1.41M); 22 years, Georgia Tech/Halford, 15 matters versus 18 years, Emory/UVA, 12 matters; Dep. refers to "Warehouse 7 in Perry," "Robert Santos," "Dr. Ananya Subramanian." Brief: "Raymond," "industrial engineering," "twenty years." Sham-affidavit doctrine, Van T. Junkins, 736 F.2d 656 (11th Cir. 1984) (verified), applies only to unexplained contradiction of clear testimony; use cautiously.
- Never addressed withheld reports (Dep. 93-95). His table (600-800 panels x $1,680) is a mitigation scenario, so salvage, overhead and mitigation reductions are not additive. Brief attributes to Decl. 7-12 quotes and points that are absent (35-45%; "end of shelf life"). Both experts' reports are dated Jan. 15, 2024 yet each reviews the other.

8. Citation and record integrity
- Barton Protective Servs. v. Faber, 274 Ga. App. 737 (2005): not located; only a Fla. 4th DCA 1999 case of that name found. Cite-check Roper (weather parenthetical doubtful), Hardin, Royal Ins., Toncee, Denton. O.C.G.A. s. 13-6-5 is mitigation; litigation expenses are s. 13-6-11 (verified; requires specific pleading and bad faith, supported by report withholding); fees also sought as "Losses" (ss. 1.7, 9.1). Restatement s. 350 is not Georgia authority. s. 13-6-8 miscited.
- Brief's SUMF cites do not match the SUMF (weather 13-14 versus 17; damages 36-40 versus 40-42; Ellington 41-43 versus 38-39). Names vary: Raymond/Marcus; Anisha/Anita; Holt "Brian"; Okafor Decl. 10 "Dr. Anita Subramanian." Brief says CEO notified Feb. 6 (SUMF 32: GC Yun) and 90-day non-renewal (LSA: 180). Santos cites (47-48) fall in discovery testimony; SUMF 30 (24:8-15) and Holt cites 22, 30, 34, 40, 52 are not in excerpts. Bar numbers differ across filings. SUMF 39 truncated.
- Brief says Okafor Decl. 8 states reporting was "fulfilled"; Decl. 8 concerns Jan. 18 and says no such thing, contradicting SUMF 25. Okafor Decl. 3-4 contain no "regional infrastructure" facts; lay weather opinion lacks foundation (Rule 56(c)(4)).

9. L.R. 56 response
- Uncontroverted SUMF facts are deemed admitted (L.R. 56, verified). Respond paragraph by paragraph: admit 25, 36; dispute 13, 14, 17, 23, 26, 30-31, 38-39, 43, 45; file counter-statement.

TIER 3 - SECONDARY

10. Damages
- Remediation $385,000: Ellington does not challenge rates (Decl. 26); Venkatesh 6.2 supports necessity.
- Feb. 6-17, 2023 "delay" (Ellington 21): Pinnacle controlled the premises; Unit 3 remained dead. LSA s. 11.5 negotiation period satisfied (demand Feb. 10; suit Mar. 17, 2023).

11. Weaknesses on our side
- Venkatesh: Zones C/D "48,000 sq ft" (LSA Ex. A: 90,000); Hargrove "VP of Operations"; relies on Holt's March 2024 testimony in a Jan. 15, 2024 report - impossible chronology (supplement); reports "Jan. 2022-Oct. 2022" versus SUMF 24 (since Jan. 2021); file labeled "Subramanian" - confirm name.
- Causation window: Holt's Nov.-Jan. readings were upper 60s-70s versus Stachybotrys threshold of about 70%; only one dated reading (78%, Oct. 3, down to 58% Oct. 11). Obtain Ex. 19, sensor data, Blackthorn invoices; the June and August outages are our best onset evidence.
- Holt's "hold off" instruction is unwritten; Okafor denies recollection; find Holt's other emails.
- Ellington's real points: $180,000 of expedited shipments to unaffected Alabama/Florida projects (Decl. 25); possible lost-profit/expedite double count; fixed-overhead measure. Retain a lost-profits expert (Venkatesh 6.4 disclaims); consider Rule 56(d) for missing discovery.

NEXT STEPS
1. Verify all Pinnacle citations; pull Hargrove, Okafor, Yun transcripts and Exs. 14, 19.
2. Calendar opposition (Aug. 5, 2024 default) and Daubert deadline; move to exclude Ellington's salvage/timing opinions.
3. File L.R. 56 response and counter-statement quoting LSA ss. 4.2, 4.3, 7.1-7.4, 9.1, 11.7 verbatim.
4. Cross-move for partial summary judgment on force majeure and s. 4.2 breach.
5. Request insurance policies; consider a candor letter on the misquotations.
6. Serve corrected supplemental Venkatesh report.
